1.grade_fit_note: Using context to choose the meaning of a multiple-meaning word fits grade 5, and map scale is taught by then.
1.note: The context ('one inch stands for ten miles') clearly supports ratio of distances; the other options are real senses of the word, which makes them good distractors.

2.grade_fit_note: Objective-case pronouns in a compound object are standard grade 6 work (L.6.1a).
2.note: The 2x2 case design is clean; 'him and I' is the strong hypercorrection lure, and 'he and me' is rarely chosen.

3.grade_fit_note: Perfect verb tenses are a grade 5 standard (L.5.1b-c).
3.note: 'By the time Ana reached' fixes a past reference point, so only the past perfect works.

4.grade_fit_note: Only one option means forceful impact, and the stem gives away the target meaning ('with great force').
4.free_elimination: A and D can be eliminated from the stem alone: 'leaned' and 'moved' carry no force, and the stem asks for force.
4.note: 'Fallen' is the only real competitor; the word 'force' in the stem points straight to 'crashed'.

5.grade_fit_note: Choosing a cause-effect transition fits grade 5.
5.note: The cleanups clearly cause the clear water; 'In addition' is the only lure a weaker reader might pick.

6.grade_fit_note: A comma after an introductory clause plus plural vs possessive is grade 5 level (L.5.2b).
6.note: A clean 2x2 design (intro comma by apostrophe); every option tests one of two known errors.

7.grade_fit_note: 'Each of' plus a plural noun, and agreement after 'there', are grade 6-7 agreement traps.
7.note: Two independent agreement decisions; the 'each of the drawings were' attraction error makes this likely harder than a typical grade 6 item.

8.grade_fit_note: A semicolon before a conjunctive adverb plus an irregular plural possessive fits grade 7.
8.note: A 2x2 design (possessive form by semicolon/comma splice); 'childrens'' is a common real error.

9.grade_fit_note: A comma for direct address plus a comma before a coordinating conjunction is grade 5-6 work.
9.note: Direct-address commas are a grade 5 standard (L.5.2c), so this sits slightly below a grade 6 target.

10.grade_fit_note: The predicate adjective after the linking verb 'smelled' is a genuine grade 7 trap.
dimensions_varied: slot 1 adverb vs adjective (modifying action verb)
slot 2 adverb vs adjective (after linking verb)
10.note: 'Cautiously / deliciously' is the strong lure for students who over-apply the -ly rule.

11.grade_fit_note: 'Especially' is a common grade 5 spelling word.
11.note: A full 2x2 design (es-/ex- by l/ll), so no option can be picked out from the option set alone.

12.grade_fit_note: Misplaced and dangling modifiers are a grade 7 standard (L.7.1c).
12.note: B (the brother is covered) and C (dangling, Leah is covered) are good lures; A is absurd enough that few will pick it.

13.grade_fit_note: A multiple-meaning word with a strong context clue fits grade 6.
13.note: 'Something no class at our school had tried before' nearly defines the word; A and C are good lures that tempt readers with the noun sense.

14.grade_fit_note: An abstract sense of 'tempered' inferred from contrast clues fits grade 7.
14.note: 'Nobody left feeling discouraged' supports softened; 'toughened' (tempered steel) and 'heated' are sophisticated lures.

15.grade_fit_note: Correlative conjunctions are a grade 5 standard (L.5.1e).
15.note: 'Decide which one we want to do' rules out the negative pair; the mismatched pairs B and C test pairing knowledge.

16.grade_fit_note: Regions vs compass directions is a classic middle-grade capitalization rule.
16.note: A clean 2x2 design; this is a well-known rule, probably slightly below a grade 7 target.

17.grade_fit_note: Inferring a theme from a character's change fits grade 6.
17.note: The narrator drops her goal of perfection to deliver all 48 cookies; B echoes Ana's rejected view, and A fits only the opening episode.

18.grade_fit_note: Inferring an unstated motive from a later action (the tape) fits grade 6.
18.note: B rests on the later tape note, but D is also defensible: Grandma offered help, was refused, and watches without stepping in, so the doorway moment alone does not decide between them.

19.grade_fit_note: Reading a character's attitude from her dialogue fits grade 6.
19.note: 'I promised cookies. Not crumbs in a bag.' states the view almost directly.

20.grade_fit_note: 'Set myself a goal' is a common, transparent phrase for grade 6.
20.note: 'Hardened' is a deliberate lure drawn from the butter context, but most readers will get 'established' at once.

21.grade_fit_note: Author's purpose for a line of dialogue fits grade 6.
21.note: B matches 'exactly what we needed'; D is vague but loosely defensible as the payoff, and C contradicts the text (the flat cookies were never broken into pieces).

22.grade_fit_note: Seasons in lower case and nationalities capitalized is a grade 5 rule.
22.note: A clean 2x2 design, but both rules are familiar, so it likely runs below the grade 5 band.

23.grade_fit_note: The 'restrict/limit' sense of 'qualified' is advanced, but the context clue makes it reachable at grade 7.
23.note: The familiar senses (certified, entitled) are strong lures, and 'described' is a plausible weak-reader pick.

24.grade_fit_note: Proper-noun capitalization plus a lowercase continuation of a split quotation fits grade 7.
24.note: A 2x2 design; the rule for capitalizing a split quotation is the harder half.

25.grade_fit_note: 'Privilege' is a classic, frequently misspelled middle-school word.
25.note: A full 2x2 design (privi/prive by -ge/-dge) with no convergence tell; 'priviledge' is the strongest lure.

26.grade_fit_note: 'Immediately' (double m, keep the e) fits grade 6 spelling.
26.note: A full 2x2 design (m/mm by -ately/-atly), so the option set gives nothing away.

27.grade_fit_note: The less common 'keep or celebrate a holiday' sense fits grade 6 with the parade clue.
27.note: 'Watches' is the strong common-sense lure; 'obeys' and 'remarks on' are real senses of the word.

28.grade_fit_note: A family title after a possessive and a short word in a book title fit grade 6.
28.note: A clean 2x2 design; both errors are common for grade 6 students.

29.grade_fit_note: A multiple-meaning word with a clear context clue fits grade 5.
29.note: 'Twice as many tomatoes' points straight to produce; 'slow down' draws on the familiar yield sign.

30.grade_fit_note: Identifying a central idea that rests on a causal claim fits grade 7.
30.note: The passage explicitly rules out the count (vote kept being put off) and the flood (no change afterward); the options are parallel and each is anchored in the text.

31.grade_fit_note: 'Raised the idea' is a common collocation, well below a grade 7 target.
31.note: 'Collected' borrows from the fundraising and 'increased' is the primary sense, but the phrase is transparent.

32.grade_fit_note: The skill level fits grade 7, but the key is stated rather than inferred.
32.note: C is stated almost word for word (he told his wife the ferry had become too risky in high water), so this is not really an inference item; A is defensible because 'changed his mind about the bridge' and 'his living mattered less' imply he once saw it as a threat to his living.

33.grade_fit_note: Explaining a paragraph's role in a causal chain fits grade 7.
33.note: B is the strong lure (the flood indirectly led to approval), but paragraph 5 explicitly says the council made no change after the flood.

34.grade_fit_note: The key repeats paragraph 2's wording verbatim, which makes it a literal recall item.
34.note: 'Saw the bridge as a threat to the ferryman's living' is lifted directly; D draws on the implied 'few families' doubt but is not attributed to most people.
